criteria.text: `GET /api/people/nobody/rising` returns 404 with `{ "error": "person not found" }` — checked manually (`curl`) or added as the first `test/server.test.ts`, since no existing route (`graph`/`sources`/`docs`) has an automated 404 test today either; `risingFor` itself only receives an already-resolved `Person`, so it cannot express this case.
Default query (`days=7`, `baseline=30`, `limit=20`, `min=3`) returns `{ days, baseline, terms }`, `terms` sorted by `lift` descending, ties broken by `term` ascending.

`count_recent` equals the raw doc count for the term in the last `days` days about the person, divided by `days`, rounded to 2 decimals. `count_baseline` equals the raw doc count in the `baseline` days immediately preceding the recent window (never overlapping it), divided by `baseline`, rounded to 2 decimals.
`lift` equals `round( (count_recent_raw / days) / ((count_baseline_raw + 1) / baseline), 2 )` exactly — pinned formula.

A term with docs only in the recent window (`count_baseline_raw = 0`) is included, with `count_baseline = 0` and a finite `lift`, and outranks a term present in both windows at a comparable recent rate.

A term whose per-day rate is the same in both windows (equal `count_recent_raw / days` and `count_baseline_raw / baseline`, tested with `days = baseline` so the smoothing effect is symmetric) has `lift` exactly `1` for the specific fixture counts pinned in the test (see Test plan) — demonstrating "stable ≈ 1" with an exact, not approximate, assertion.
`min` filters on the raw recent count: with `min` above a term's raw recent doc count, that term is excluded even though it would otherwise qualify; lowering `min` includes it again.
The person's own alias tokens never appear as a `term` in the response.

`kind`, `source`, `domain` behave like the equivalent parameters on `graph`/`docs`: an unrecognized value falls back to `all`; a recognized value filters both the recent and baseline windows identically.
A person with no docs, or a `days` window with no docs, returns `{ days, baseline, terms: [] }`, not an error.
`limit` clamps the returned array to at most `limit` rows (default 20), verified with a fixture that has more than `limit` qualifying terms or by asserting the clamp on an out-of-range input.
Manual: in `design-5.html`, checking "em alta (7d)" adds a gold ring to the matching atlas nodes without changing their fill color or radius, and unchecking removes it.
Manual: the "em alta" side list shows at most 10 rows with a `×`-suffixed lift value, in pt-BR, and shows `carregando…` while the request is in flight and `nada em alta agora` when `terms` is empty.
